In each turn, Pink Panther chooses a row or column and paints all its cells pink (regardless of whether they were white or pink). In each turn, Mr. White chooses consecutive cells on a row or column and paints them white.

If at any stage after Mr. White's turn, at least cells are pink, Pink Panther wins. Otherwise, the game continues. Find the largest value in terms of for which Pink Panther can be certain to win in a finite number of turns, regardless of Mr. White's play.

Given natural numbers $n, k$, Pink Panther and Mr. White play on an $n \times n$ board in turns. Initially, all cells are white. Pink Panther starts. In each turn, Pink Panther chooses a row or column and paints all its cells pink (regardless of whether they were white or pink). In each turn, Mr. White chooses $n-1$ consecutive cells on a row or column and paints them white.

If at any stage after Mr. White's turn, at least $k$ cells are pink, Pink Panther wins. Otherwise, the game continues. Find the largest value in terms of $n$ for which Pink Panther can be certain to win in a finite number of turns, regardless of Mr. White's play.
